{{short description|Tunisian physicist and politician}}
{{expand French|date=May 2024|topic=bio}}
[[File:Fouzia Charfi (21e Maghreb des Livres, Paris, 7 et 8 février 2015).jpg|thumb|right|Faouzia Charfi in 2015]]
'''Faouzia Farida Charfi''' (born 1941 in [[Sfax]], {{nee}} '''Rekik''') is a [[Tunisia]]n scientist, intellectual and politician. She was Minister of State for Education in 2011.

==Life==
Charfi graduated from the [[University of Paris|Sorbonne]], [[Paris]], in 1963 in physical sciences, then gained doctorates in 1978 and 1984 from the {{ill|Faculty of Science of Tunis|fr|Faculté des sciences de Tunis}} which is part of [[Tunis El Manar University]].<ref name=culture /> She became the Tunisian Minister of State for Education in 2011.<ref name="culture">{{cite web |title=Faouzia Charfi |url=https://www.franceculture.fr/personne-faouzia-charfi |publisher=France Culture |accessdate=1 June 2019}}</ref><ref name="inter">{{cite web |title=Faouzia Farida Charfi |url=https://www.franceinter.fr/personnes/faouzia-farida-charfi |publisher=France Inter |accessdate=1 June 2019}}</ref><ref name="boukhayatia">{{cite news |last1=Boukhayatia |first1=Rihab |title=L'universitaire et intellectuelle tunisienne Faouzia Charfi honorée à l'IMA, à Paris |url=https://www.huffpostmaghreb.com/entry/lintellectuelle-tunisienne-faouzia-charfi-honoree-a-lima-a-paris_mg_5c6d6835e4b0f40774cad671 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190220231019/https://www.huffpostmaghreb.com/entry/lintellectuelle-tunisienne-faouzia-charfi-honoree-a-lima-a-paris_mg_5c6d6835e4b0f40774cad671 |url-status=usurped |archive-date=February 20, 2019 |accessdate=1 June 2019 |work=Huffpost |date=20 February 2019}}</ref><ref name="samoud">{{cite news |last1=Samoud |first1=Wafa |title=Selon Faouzia Charfi, "L'islam politique ne reconnaît pas la pensée rationnelle" |work=Huffpost |date=27 March 2018}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1997 she was appointed a [[Chevalier de la Légion d’Honneur]], and in 2001 a [[Commandeur des Palmes Académiques]].<ref name=culture /> In 2019 she was awarded the Chair's medal of the [[Arab World Institute]] in recognition of her work against [[islamic fundamentalism]].<ref name=kapitalis /><ref name=boukhayatia />

==Personal life==
Charfi's husband was [[Mohamed Charfi]] (1936–2008), a Tunisian academic and politician.<ref name="kapitalis">{{cite news |title=Paris: Hommage de l'Institut du monde arabe à Faouzia Charfi |url=http://kapitalis.com/tunisie/2019/02/20/paris-hommage-de-linstitut-du-monde-arabe-a-faouzia-charfi/ |accessdate=1 June 2019 |work=Kapitalis |date=20 February 2019}}</ref>
